literal: enduring life having protected compassion to those who practice is not they say one's own life fearing deed
translation: They say there are no fearful consequences for the lives of those who protect other living beings and practice compassion.
modern: நிலைபெற்ற பிற உயிர்களைப் பாதுகாத்து அருள் உள்ளத்தோடு வாழ்பவர்களுக்கு, தம்முடைய உயிர் அஞ்சும்படியான துன்பச் செயல்கள் இல்லை என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவர்.
explanation: This couplet states that practicing compassion towards others is the ultimate protection for oneself. The phrase 'man uyir ompi' means protecting the enduring lives of all beings, while 'arul alvarkku' refers to those who actively practice compassion. The text asserts that such people will never encounter deeds ('vinai') that cause their own lives to fear ('tan uyir ancum'). By shielding others from harm, a compassionate person naturally shields their own life from fearful consequences.
